summary:
AgriORBIT is an interactive, NASA-powered agricultural decision-support prototype developed by our team to help Filipino farmers adapt to changing climate conditions.

Focused on Botolan, Zambales, Philippines, our project transforms NASA POWER historical climate data into understandable information for climate-resilient crop planning.

AgriORBIT compares three crop-rotation scenarios: Rice–Rice, Rice–Mungbean, and Corn–Mungbean. It analyzes historical rainfall, dry spells, and seasonal variability while considering farmer-reported irrigation, soil conditions, and planting schedules.

Our system combines an interactive 3D dashboard with a scientific analysis workspace, allowing users to explore different farming scenarios. It includes data-quality checks, NASA source information, and transparent scientific limitations.

Rather than predicting crop yields or prescribing a single planting choice, AgriORBIT helps farmers identify climate-related risks and important field conditions requiring further evaluation.

Through teamwork in software engineering, data science, and interactive design, we aim to make NASA Earth observation data more accessible and useful to agricultural communities.

Our long-term vision is to develop AgriORBIT into a practical, scientifically validated climate-resilience platform for farmers.
details:
AgriORBIT: NASA-Powered Climate Resilience for Farming

Project Overview

AgriORBIT is an interactive agricultural decision-support prototype developed by our team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" by helping farmers understand historical climate conditions and explore crop-rotation strategies.

How It Works

Focused on Botolan, Zambales, Philippines, AgriORBIT uses NASA POWER historical meteorological data and farmer-reported conditions to compare three crop rotations: Rice–Rice, Rice–Mungbean, and Corn–Mungbean.

The system analyzes rainfall, seasonal variability, and historical dry spells across planting seasons from 2015–2024. It presents understandable comparisons to help farmers identify climate-related risks and important field conditions requiring verification.

Innovation and Technology

Our team developed an interactive 3D mission-control dashboard, combining scientific analysis with engaging visualizations.

We used Python, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, NASA POWER APIs, GitHub, and Render. The scientific engine includes data-quality checks, source records, and conditional FAO-56 evapotranspiration calculations.

Scientific Validity

AgriORBIT distinguishes NASA observations from synthetic demonstrations and withholds calculations when required information is incomplete. It does not claim to predict yields, certify crop suitability, or guarantee water savings. Further local soil measurements and farmer validation are required.

Impact and Team Collaboration

Through collaboration in software engineering, data science, scientific research, and interface design, our team aims to make NASA climate evidence more accessible to Filipino farmers.

Our long-term goal is to develop AgriORBIT into a scientifically validated agricultural decision-support platform.

Our Vision: Turning NASA climate evidence into understandable information for more resilient farming.
